title: Even mystical-symbolic image-cult is moral sin—Decalogue binds all men forever against exposing God’s likenesses for cult
source_text: XXII. Ex quibus patet gentium sapientes gravissime peccasse, quum Deum expresserant sub variis figuris, & in iis colendum illum proposuerunt, etiamsi mysticam & symbolicam tantum significationem fictitiis illis tribuerent: adeoque non lege positiva duntaxat, sed morali, quae omnes homines perpetuo obligat, in Decalogo prohiberi, ne ullae Dei similitudines, ut nec cujusquam alterius rei, ad cultum exponantur.
pass_a_gloss: From which it is plain that the wise of the Gentiles sinned most gravely when they had expressed God under various figures, and proposed him to be cultivated in them, even if they attributed only a mystical and symbolic signification to those fictive things: and accordingly not by a positive law only, but by a moral one, which perpetually obliges all men, it is prohibited in the Decalogue that any likenesses of God, as neither of any other thing, be exposed for cult.
pass_b_english: Symbolic paganism still counts as grave sin—mystical intention does not sanitize image-cult.
The Decalogue’s ban is moral and perpetual for every human likeness set out for cult.

choices.why: Crafted figures, not found idols only.
